messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int sd(int n) { if (n == 0) return 0; return n % 10 + sd(n); }

Question: What is sd(25)?
The student answered: 7

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The recursive call moves toward the base case on its own

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: long-winded, walks through the steps one by one, 20 to 35 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["First n is 25, so 25 mod 10 gives 5, then the function calls itself again with n getting smaller each time until it hits zero, adding 2 and returning 7.", "n equals 25, not zero, so take last digit 5, then call sd again and this time n becomes 2, add 2 to get 7.", "So sd(25) returns 25 mod 10 which is 5 plus sd(25), but the second call uses a reduced n that becomes 2, so 5 plus 2 is 7.", "Start with n as 25, remainder is 5, recursive call keeps going automatically toward zero, so next n is 2, adding 5 and 2 to get 7.", "The base case is n equals zero, 25 is not zero so remainder 5, then the call repeats with n dropping to 2, giving 5 plus 2 equals 7."]}

sentences: First n is 25, so 25 mod 10 gives 5, then the function calls itself again with n getting smaller each time until it hits zero, adding 2 and returning 7.
n equals 25, not zero, so take last digit 5, then call sd again and this time n becomes 2, add 2 to get 7.
So sd(25) returns 25 mod 10 which is 5 plus sd(25), but the second call uses a reduced n that becomes 2, so 5 plus 2 is 7.
Start with n as 25, remainder is 5, recursive call keeps going automatically toward zero, so next n is 2, adding 5 and 2 to get 7.
The base case is n equals zero, 25 is not zero so remainder 5, then the call repeats with n dropping to 2, giving 5 plus 2 equals 7.
